gap: No result ChatGPT got says what each filament changer cannot feed. Bambu's AMS 2 Pro rejects generic TPU and any carbon- or glass-fibre filament except three Bambu CF grades. Creality's CFS rejects all TPU but accepts PA-CF. The QIDI Box rejects generic TPU and TPU 95A but accepts ABS-, PLA- and PETG-CF/GF and PPS-CF. On all three, flexible filament has to bypass the changer.
standout_why: I compared against desktop3dprinters.us/lists/multicolor-enclosed-3d-printers (cited by ChatGPT, verified 2026-10-30) and speakcad.com/blog/best-enclosed-3d-printer (top result). Both cover purge waste: desktop3dprinters quotes Bambu's wiki on flushing at every change, and speakcad says AMS, ACE Pro and CFS purge at each change. Neither says which filaments a changer can or cannot feed. desktop3dprinters 'does not mention TPU or carbon fiber' and says nothing about drying. speakcad covers neither TPU/CF limits nor where the units sit or whether they heat. The other cited page, 3dprinterlist.com, could not be opened (certificate error), so I could not compare against it.
decides: Many shoppers want an enclosure so they can print ABS, ASA, nylon and fibre-filled filaments, so this can change the pick. Among the units checked, the Bambu AMS 2 Pro (P2S Combo, H2D Combo) is the most restrictive for fibre-filled filament: it takes only Bambu PLA-CF, PAHT-CF and PETG-CF and rejects 'other filaments that contain carbon fiber or glass fiber'. It also 'cannot dry completely' ABS, ASA, PA and PC at its 65 °C maximum. Creality's CFS on the K2 Pro and K2 Plus accepts PA-CF. The QIDI Box on the Q2, Plus5 and Max4 (all three already on Dealectric) accepts ABS-CF/GF, PLA-CF/GF, PETG-CF/GF and PPS-CF, but not QIDI PAHT-CF, and dries at up to 65 °C while printing. For multi-colour PLA or PETG work, ChatGPT's Bambu pick still stands. For multi-material jobs with third-party CF/GF, a CFS or QIDI Box printer can feed what the AMS 2 Pro cannot. TPU 95A has to come from a separate spool holder on all three, so no combo makes 'multiple filaments' include standard flexibles.

findings.product: Bambu Lab AMS 2 Pro (P2S Combo, H2D Combo)
findings.label: Filaments the AMS 2 Pro does not support
findings.value: TPE, generic TPU, damp PVA, damp BVOH, Bambu PET-CF, Bambu TPU 95A, and other filaments that contain carbon fiber or glass fiber
findings.source_title: Bambu Lab AMS 2 Pro - Automatic Material System | MatterHackers
findings.note: Bambu's own store (us.store.bambulab.com) and wiki returned HTTP 402 to automated reads. This is a named US retailer's reproduction of Bambu's 'Filament Supported / Filament Not Supported' table, and the page does not say it was copied from Bambu.

findings.product: Bambu Lab AMS 2 Pro (P2S Combo, H2D Combo)
findings.label: Filaments the AMS 2 Pro supports
findings.value: PLA, PETG, ABS, ASA, PET, PA, PC, PVA (dried), BVOH (dried), PP, POM, HIPS, Bambu PLA-CF / PAHT-CF / PETG-CF / Support for PLA/PETG, TPU for AMS
findings.source_title: Bambu Lab AMS 2 Pro - Automatic Material System | MatterHackers
findings.note: The only fibre-filled filaments it accepts are those three Bambu grades. The only TPU it accepts is Bambu's 'TPU for AMS'.

findings.product: Bambu Lab AMS 2 Pro (P2S Combo, H2D Combo)
findings.label: Maximum drying temperature, and the filaments it cannot fully dry
findings.value: 65 °C; the page says 'These filaments require a higher drying temperature. The AMS 2 Pro cannot dry them completely' and lists ABS, ASA, PET, PA, PC, PVA, BVOH, POM, HIPS, Bambu PLA-CF, PAHT-CF, PETG-CF and TPU for AMS
findings.source_title: Bambu Lab AMS 2 Pro - Automatic Material System | MatterHackers
findings.note: These are the engineering materials people usually buy an enclosure for. Same retailer reproduction of Bambu's table as above.

findings.product: Creality CFS (K2 Pro Combo, K2 Plus Combo)
findings.label: Filaments the CFS supports and does not support
findings.value: Supports 'most filaments such as PLA, PETG, ABS, ASA, PA-CF'. Not supported: 'flexible filaments such as TPU and damp PVA, BVOH'. Also: 'No, CFS does not support TPU.' TPU goes on the K2 Plus's standard spool holder instead.
findings.source_title: Creality K2 Plus & CFS Frequently Asked Questions You Should Know | Creality Forum
findings.note: Posted by the official CREALITY account on 2024-11-12 about the original CFS. The same CFS ships in the K2 Pro Combo. I could not read the CFS 2 table, which may differ.

findings.label: Filaments the QIDI Box supports
findings.value: PLA, PETG, ABS, ASA, PET, PA, PC, PVA (dried), BVOH (dried), PP, POM, HIPS, TPU 64D, plus carbon- and glass-filled grades. The QIDI product-page search result spelled these out as ABS-CF/GF, PLA-CF/GF, PETG-CF/GF, PPS-CF and PET-CF/GF.
findings.source_title: QIDI Box: A Complete Guide to QIDI's New Multi-Color and Filament Management System | QIDI
findings.note: QIDI's own blog, dated 2025-08-25 by ChloeAustin, with prices referencing September 2026, so it has been updated since. The blog lists the base materials and says 'carbon- and glass-filled variants'. The exact CF/GF grades come from the search result for the qidi3d.com QIDI Box product page, which returned HTTP 429 when I tried to open it.

findings.label: Filaments the QIDI Box does not support
findings.value: TPE, generic TPU, TPU 95A, damp PVA, damp BVOH, QIDI PAHT-CF, some silk grades, glow-in-the-dark PLA, unusually rigid or soft filaments; no cardboard spools
findings.source_title: QIDI Box: A Complete Guide to QIDI's New Multi-Color and Filament Management System | QIDI
findings.note: Recommended spools are plastic, 50–72 mm wide and 195–202 mm in diameter, or use a spool adapter.

findings.label: Compatible printers and drying temperature
findings.value: Q2C, Q2, Plus 5 and Max4 list QIDI Box support on their spec sheets (the Plus4 needs its own hub and cable parts). Dries at up to 65 °C, and 'drying runs at the same time as printing'.
findings.source_title: QIDI Box: A Complete Guide to QIDI's New Multi-Color and Filament Management System | QIDI
findings.note: The page says the Box's drying temperature is separate from the printer's 65 °C chamber heating.

findings.label: What the cited rival page says about filament limits
findings.value: desktop3dprinters.us lists 23 enclosed multi-material printers with nozzle count, chamber temperature and filament unit, and says nothing about TPU, carbon fibre or drying
findings.source_title: Multicolor 3D printers with an enclosure: every enclosed multi-material model | Desktop 3D Printers
findings.note: Published 2026-10-28, verified 2026-10-30. Its only mechanism point is the single-nozzle flush versus two-nozzle swap.
